written.myAnswer: Measurement is the comparison of an unknown quantity with an accepted standard quantity. Its two parts are a numerical value and a unit.
A standard unit ensures measurements are consistent and comparable, avoiding confusion when different people measure the same quantity.
Base quantities: length, mass and time. Derived quantities: speed, volume and density.
A standard system enables a tailor to take and use measurements consistently, helping clothes fit properly and avoiding confusion.
A standard unit makes measurements consistent and comparable, so different people obtain the same result without confusion.

Base quantities are selected as fundamental quantities; derived quantities are expressed in terms of one or more base quantities. The SI base units are metre (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K), mole (mol) and candela (cd).
